newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi confirms it will sell Pioneer DVD players.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi confirms it will sell Pioneer DVD players.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd confirmed on Friday a newspaper report that it would sell digital video disc (DVD) players made by Pioneer Electronic Corp under the Hitachi brand name instead of producing them itself.
"We will sell DVD players to be provided by Pioneer, but we cannot provide the details of the launch of those players," a Hitachi spokeswoman said.
"We have not decided if we will continue selling Pioneer-made players in the future or if we will produce our own players," she added.

The industrial daily Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun reported on Thursday that Hitachi had decided to sell Pioneer DVD players because Hitachi did not think there would be many DVD software titles available on the market soon.
But the Hitachi spokeswoman said the company made the decision for a different reason.

"We will focus more on the development of DVD-ROM (read-only memory) drives ourselves. But we also know that DVD players will be important in terms of our sales strategy so we made that decision," she said. Pioneer officials were not immediately available for comment.
DVD is a new recording system which has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs obsolete.
Electronics manufacturers such as Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd and Toshiba Corp have said they would produce DVD players and launch them in November.
